recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. The authoritative core Quantity datatype source already implements the accepted request; future work should only be considered if FHIR-I changes the UCUM annotation policy or adopts a broader invariant-test convention.
issue_request: FHIR-42788 was an Applied/Persuasive FHIR-I change request, raised in R5 and applied for R6, asking FHIR core to document the IG Publisher warning that UCUM codes with human-readable annotations such as {Z-Score} can be misleading and that Quantity.unit should carry human-readable unit text. The reporter also asked for invariant tests.
initial_application: Git commit 744e8befa99ad87fd2853b7612a0eb6b082b8bb5 applied the issue by adding qty-4 to source/datatypes/quantity.xml with best-practice severity, the requested Quantity.code FHIRPath expression, explanatory warning text, and source/observation/invariant-tests/qty-4.f1.fail.xml as an annotated UCUM negative test fixture.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes from 2024-03-18 record a motion to accept FHIR-42788 as a request to put an IG Publisher warning into the specification. The origin Zulip thread explains that UCUM annotations are legal but often misunderstood as meaningful, and that FHIR has Quantity.unit for human-readable display text. FHIR-33063 is the same UCUM annotation guidance family and is already represented on the combined branch, so it was not decided again.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/fhir.ini lists Quantity as an active normative datatype, source/datatypes/quantity.xml already has the best-practice invariant and explanation, source/observation/invariant-tests/qty-4.f1.fail.xml already exercises an annotated UCUM code, and the current rendered build exposes the qty-4 guideline.
